title: Upfly configuration
description: The settings Upfly reads from upfly.config.json, or from what upfly.config.ts exports, in the folder a command runs on. Every setting is optional.

$schema.description: The schema an editor checks this file against. Upfly reads nothing from it.

publicDirs.description: The folders the site is served from, relative to this file, such as ["public"]. ["."] is this folder itself, as for a plain HTML site. A root-relative path such as /hero.png is looked up in them. Setting them replaces Upfly's own detection, and --public replaces them for one run.

items.patternErrorMessage: Write a folder inside the project, such as public, or . for the project itself: not an absolute path, a drive, or a path that goes up with ..

publicPolicy.description: What optimize does with an original image once it is converted. "replace", the default, removes it once every reference to it has moved to the new file and no file Upfly reads still names it. "keep-original" leaves it beside the new file; --keep-originals does the same for one run.

format.description: The format images are converted to. "avif" is the other choice, which some older browsers cannot show. --format overrides it for one run.

exclude.description: Paths to leave out of every run, in .gitignore syntax, relative to this file. They add to the patterns in .upflyignore and to any --exclude.

check.description: What upfly check holds the project to, and what fails it.

maxImageBytes.description: The largest an image in use may be, in bytes, such as 500000. upfly check fails when an image a reference uses is larger, unless failOn leaves too-large out; an image nothing uses never fails it.

failOn.description: What fails upfly check: "broken", a reference to an image that does not exist; "too-large", an image in use larger than maxImageBytes; "possibly-broken", an image path in code or data that names no file. Unset, it fails on broken, and on too-large when maxImageBytes is set; [] makes it fail on nothing. An unused image never fails it. --fail-on replaces it for one run, and --warn makes nothing fail.

watch.description: How an editor that watches the project for new images treats them, as the Upfly VS Code extension does. Upfly's commands watch nothing: they check these settings and act on none.

folders.description: The folders watched for new images, relative to this file, such as ["public"]; ["."] is the whole project.

items.patternErrorMessage: Write a folder inside the project, such as public, or . for the project itself: not an absolute path, a drive, or a path that goes up with ..

skip.description: Folders inside the watched ones where no new image is converted, relative to this file, such as ["public/vendor"].

items.patternErrorMessage: Write a folder inside the project, such as public, or . for the project itself: not an absolute path, a drive, or a path that goes up with ..

keepOriginals.description: true keeps each converted image's original beside it; by default only the new file is kept, its original removed once it is provably not needed.

outside.description: "replace" treats an image that arrives from outside the editor, such as one an agent or a download writes, as one pasted in it: its original is removed once it is converted. Without it, such an original stays until no line names it.
